docs.title: tappack
docs.text: tappack builds a Tasmota Berry project into a .tapp package. It reads a manifest.yaml, collects the project files and declared dependencies, applies channel-specific version patches, generates autoexec.be, and writes the resulting archive.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install tappack

For a one-shot run without a separate install:

uvx tappack --help

docs.title: Package a project
docs.text:
The repository includes a runnable example. From its examples directory, build it with:

cd docs/examples
tappack --module-path sample_app --output ./sample_app.tapp --channel-id development

tappack also accepts a project path from elsewhere. Run tappack --help for its options; see the quick start and manifest guide for details.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Read the tappack documentation for installation, CLI usage, manifest fields, and deployment guidance.

docs.title: Serving and remote access
docs.text:
tappack creates .tapp files; it no longer starts a web server or opens a tunnel. The former server feature was convenient during development, but it coupled an artifact builder to a long-running web process and a public-network tunnel. That added dependencies and operational behavior that packaging itself does not need, while making it easier to expose project files unintentionally.

Keep the responsibilities separate: build the archive with tappack, then publish it through a deployment or static-hosting workflow you already control. For temporary remote device access, use a separately managed tunnel tool such as tailcat rather than embedding tunnel lifecycle and exposure decisions in the packager.

The packaging command and manifest behavior are documented in the quick start and manifest reference.

docs.title: Manifest reference
docs.text:
A project can contain a manifest.yaml at its root. tappack searches upward from --module-path for this file. If no manifest is found, it packages the directory using its name and does not resolve dependencies or patches.

The manifest describes the package name, startup behavior, dependencies, and optional version patches. The runnable sample is embedded in the quick start.

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning name string Package name used in the generated autoexec.be and as the default output filename. If omitted, the project directory name is used. autoexec object Controls the generated startup file. dependencies mapping Maps package subdirectory names to dependency sources. patches list File changes applied while packaging, including channel-specific version updates.

tappack generates autoexec.be from the package's Berry file paths. Set autoexec.import: true to import the package during startup; the default is false. Use .channels to override autoexec settings for a channel, as in the sample manifest.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Each entry under dependencies is keyed by the directory name where that dependency is placed in the package. Supported source forms are:

Source Fields URL A URL string, or an object with .type: URL and url; the target must be a .tapp archive. Local path .type: LocalPath and path; the directory is packaged recursively. The path is resolved from the process's current working directory. GitHub release asset .type: GitHubReleaseAsset, org, repo, and filename; optionally set version and prefix. If version is omitted, the latest release is used. The default tag prefix is v.

For a local dependency, invoke tappack from the directory that makes the manifest's path resolve correctly. In the repository example, the command runs from docs/examples, so path: shared_library selects the sibling directory.

A complete example of a channel-specific local dependency and version patch is in the sample manifest.

When a dependency contains only channel entries and the selected channel is not present, it is skipped. A direct source may also provide .channels; those entries replace the direct source when they match.

docs.title: Version patches
docs.text:
A patch entry uses .type: Version and includes a project-relative path and a regular-expression pattern containing {version}. The matched semantic version's patch component is increased by inc_patch (default 1), then the selected channel and a build timestamp are added. Patches can be placed beneath .channels to apply them only to selected release channels.

The sample manifest patches src/version.be for the development channel. With no matching channel patch, no patch is applied.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Install tappack from PyPI:

pip install tappack

The repository contains a complete sample project and a local dependency. From the examples directory, package it with a channel-specific version patch:

cd docs/examples
tappack --module-path sample_app --output ./sample_app.tapp --channel-id development

The command writes sample_app.tapp in the current directory. The manifest, Berry sources, and generated autoexec.be are stored in the archive; the local dependency is placed under the shared/ directory.

The example manifest is a real file used by the command above:

name: sample_app
autoexec:
  import: false
  .channels:
    development:
      import: true
dependencies:
  shared:
    .type: LocalPath
    path: shared_library
patches:
  - .channels:
      development:
        .type: Version
        path: src/version.be
        pattern: "var VERSION = '{version}'"

docs.title: CLI options
docs.text:
• --module-path selects the project directory. It defaults to the current directory.
  • --output selects the .tapp file. If omitted, the manifest name is used as the filename; when no manifest is present, the project directory name is used. The output is written in the current directory.
  • --channel-id selects channel-specific dependency, autoexec, and patch settings.

The same scalar settings can be supplied through TAPPACK__MODULE_PATH, TAPPACK__OUTPUT, and TAPPACK__CHANNEL_ID. For example, from docs/examples:

TAPPACK__MODULE_PATH=sample_app TAPPACK__CHANNEL_ID=development tappack --output ./sample_app.tapp

Corio settings can also load a dotenv file selected with --env or a YAML file selected with --config; CLI options take precedence over environment, dotenv, and YAML values.

For an ephemeral invocation, run the same command with uvx tappack instead of tappack. Run tappack --help to see the available options.

For the manifest field reference and dependency forms, continue to the manifest guide. For the rationale behind packaging-only scope, see deployment guidance.
